question: Can a subsampling-aware criticality analysis distinguish genuine population-dynamics structure from analysis/sampling artifacts in Allen Neuropixels spontaneous recordings without merely rediscovering known subsampling sensitivity?
dataset: Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels
external_reserve: 32 brain_observatory_1.1 sessions; earlier 16/16 design-only split superseded before any spike values were read because its spontaneous periods are fragmented/interleaved
split_amendment: Revised from brain_observatory_1.1 to functional_connectivity after design-only NWB interval inspection and primary-source check showed a standardized continuous ~30-min spontaneous block in functional_connectivity; no spike values had been read.
holdout_note: Procedural holdout only; public data and model pretraining are not a secure blindness boundary.
eligibility_rule: Session must have >=32 Allen metadata quality=good VISp units before spike access.
primary_observed_population: 32 good VISp units selected deterministically from each eligible mouse/session; unit-subset sensitivity must be empirically calibrated.
current_method_status: Stopped: aggregate/binomial MR calibration passes, but one real discovery mouse shows neuron-subset-dependent applicability; static fixed-neuron heterogeneity, mixed module timescales, and simple state-switch stress tests do not reproduce the low-R2 failures. Further rescue would be adaptive model expansion.
stop_reason: The first discovery mouse violates the calibrated single-timescale MR applicability model in a subset-dependent way not reproduced by prespecified branching stress tests; continuing would require post-outcome model invention in a mature debate.
